situation: Want to write a LinkedIn recommendation for Marco, who was my direct report for 2 years as a customer support lead. He built our help center from scratch and cut ticket volume a lot.
reply: I managed Marco for two years while he led our customer support team. He built our help center from nothing, 140 articles in his first six months, and ticket volume dropped by about 35 percent as a result. What stood out was how he trained new agents: patient, practical, and always with real tickets. I'd hire him again tomorrow.
note: How you know him, two strengths with numbers, a clear endorsement. Short enough for LinkedIn.

situation: 以前实习时带过的学生小韩请我给她写出国读研的推荐信，但她只在我们组待了两个月，工作一般，我觉得写不出有分量的东西。想婉拒。
reply: 小韩，谢谢你想到我，也祝申请顺利。认真想了一下，我觉得我不是最合适的推荐人，我们一起工作只有两个月，能写的具体内容有限，反而可能拖累你的材料。你毕设的指导老师看到你的时间更长，应该能给你一封更有力的推荐信。
note: 写不出强推荐就趁早温和地拒绝，比写一封平淡的信对她更好。

situation: Getting a reference call Thursday for my ex-colleague Sam, who's applying for an ops manager job. His vendor negotiations were great but he struggled to manage his one direct report. They'll probably ask about people management.
reply: On people management, I can only speak to a small part of it: Sam had one direct report for about eight months, and he found giving tough feedback hard early on. Where he really stood out was vendor negotiation. He renegotiated our three biggest logistics contracts and saved about $220,000 a year, while keeping every one of those relationships friendly.
note: Narrow the scope instead of stretching the truth: answer the weakness briefly and factually, then give the strongest true evidence.

situation: 家里请了四年的住家阿姨刘姐，因为我们要搬去上海，她想在北京找新雇主，请我写一段推荐发给中介。她做饭好、带孩子特别细心，有一次孩子半夜高烧是她发现的。
reply: 刘桂芳大姐在我们家做住家阿姨四年，从2022年10月到今年10月，主要负责做饭和照顾两个孩子。她特别细心：有一次半夜小儿子发高烧，是她起来查看时发现的，马上叫醒我们，处理得很冷静。她做饭讲究营养搭配，两个孩子挑食的毛病都是她慢慢带好的。我们因为搬家才不得不分开，非常放心地推荐她。如需了解，欢迎联系我：139 1024 5678。
note: 私人推荐也要写清认识多久、做什么，再用一两个具体的事说话，最后给联系方式。不写她的年龄、家庭或身体情况。

situation: I'm a small landlord. My tenant of 3 years, Aisha Bello, is moving to Manchester at the end of October and her new letting agent emailed asking for a reference. Rent always on time, and she handled a burst pipe last winter brilliantly.
reply: Hello, I'm happy to give a reference for Aisha Bello. She has rented my one-bedroom flat at 14 Grove Road since October 2023, and I've managed the tenancy myself throughout. In those three years her rent of £1,150 a month has been paid on time every month. When a pipe burst in the kitchen last winter, she shut off the water, called me within minutes and kept a photo log for the insurer, which saved us both a great deal of trouble. I'd let to her again without hesitation, and you're welcome to call me on 07700 900318. Best regards, Martin Hale
note: A landlord reference is still how you know them, specific evidence, and a clear endorsement; stick to what a letting agent actually needs and nothing personal.

situation: My former manager Dana was just laid off in a restructure and is job hunting. I want to write her a LinkedIn recommendation. She managed me for 3 years at Quill, pushed me into my first conference talk, and got our team through a messy platform migration without losing anyone.
reply: Dana managed me for three years on the data team at Quill, and she is the best manager I've had. She led our team of seven through a platform migration that ran four months over, and nobody left, which says a lot about how she treats people under pressure. She also saw something in me before I did: she pushed me to give my first conference talk and spent two evenings rehearsing it with me. Any team hiring a hands-on engineering manager would be lucky to have her.
note: Upward recommendations carry weight because the writer was the one managed: one example about delivery, one about people. Leave the layoff out.

situation: My former colleague Jordan asked for a LinkedIn recommendation and sent me a draft to post. Most of it is fair, but it says he 'led our platform strategy', which was actually our director Nadia's call. I don't want to sign something untrue or make it awkward.
reply: Happy to do this, Jordan. I've tweaked your draft so it's all things I saw myself. I kept the vendor onboarding numbers and the bit about the March outage, both spot on. I swapped 'led our platform strategy' for 'drove the platform rollout across four regional teams', since the strategy was Nadia's call and a hiring manager could easily check. That line is true and still strong. If you're good with it, I'll post it tonight.
note: When someone drafts their own reference, edit to what you can stand behind and say why in one line; offering a strong true replacement keeps it from feeling like a rejection.

situation: I teach AP Chemistry. My student Jaylen Brooks asked me for a letter for the Hartwell STEM Scholarship, due Oct 15. I taught him two years and supervised his project testing lead in the district's drinking fountains. He wants to study environmental engineering.
reply:
Dear Scholarship Committee,
I'm pleased to recommend Jaylen Brooks for the Hartwell STEM Scholarship. I taught Jaylen AP Chemistry for two years at Lincoln High and supervised his independent project on lead in our district's drinking fountains. He tested 62 fountains across nine schools, found three above the EPA action level, and presented the results to the school board, which replaced all three within a month. In class he is the student others turn to when they're stuck, and he explains without making anyone feel slow. I recommend him without hesitation for a degree in environmental engineering, and I'd be glad to talk further: 555-014-2290 or m.ortiz@lincolnhs.org.
Sincerely,
Maria Ortiz
note: Academic letter: how you know him, one project with numbers and a real outcome, one trait with an example, then an endorsement tied to what he'll study.
